text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London continued to move higher on trade and commission house buying. August added $3.80 to close at $327.90 per tonne, while October closed $4.50 higher at $318.90. Raw sugar futures in New York settled at their highest level in five-weeks amid fresh fund buying. Today's gains were technically-driven as there seems to be no fundamental reason for a rise in sugar prices. July closed 17 points higher at 11.34 cents/lb. October ended 19 points higher at 11.19 cents/lb. The outer months gained between 8 and 14 points.

SUDAN - Sugar production in Sudan in 1997/98 (November/April) is forecast to reach 555,000 tonnes, white value, up from 505,000 tonnes in 1996/97 and 459,196 tonnes in 1995/96. Offtake in 1997/98 is forecast at 410,000 tonnes, up from 400,000 tonnes in 1996/97 and 385,000 tonnes in 1995/96.

POLAND - Sugar imports in February 1997 amounted to 12,435 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 1,613 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first six months of 1996/97 (September/February) up to 53,898 tonnes against 68,258 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 85,306 tonnes against 100,248 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in September/February 1996/97 were the Czech Republic with 16,423 tonnes whites against nil and Germany with 15,389 tonnes compared to 8,765 tonnes.

Sugar exports in February 1997 amounted to 19,434 tonnes against negligible amounts in February 1996. This brought cumulative exports in September/February 1996/97 up to 192,596 tonnes, up from 2,163 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 4,440 tonnes against 14,828 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Germany with 23,519 tonnes whites against nil, Algeria with 23,279 tonnes against nil, Syria with 28,189 tonnes raws against nil and Algeria with 18,450 tonnes raws, up from 288 tonnes.

Pakistan has issued a buying tender for 50,000 tonnes of white sugar in two equal shipments. The first tender will be held on July 31 and the second on August 15. Details of the exact shipment periods have yet to emerge. Taiwan will hold a buying tender for 18,000 tonnes of white sugar on June 6 for shipment July 17/31. No further details were immediately available. Iran bought 30,000 tonnes of raw sugar at $280 per tonne for shipment in August.
